newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Industrialising Malaysia to unveil local motorcycle.
newsitem.headline: Industrialising Malaysia to unveil local motorcycle.

text.p: Malaysia will officially unveil its national motorcycle on Thursday, capping another milestone in the country's industrialisation plan of making vehicles with foreign help, industry analysts said on Wednesday.
The motorcycle launch follows the 13-year success of the popular Proton cars, which have since been joined by a second Malaysian-made car and two national van projects.
The Southeast Asian country, which aims to be an industrialised nation by 2020, has also announced plans to build made-in-Malaysia buses and trucks.

"To industrialise, you need more than manufacturing. Like the developed countries, you need heavy industries which provide jobs, transfer of technology," said Irene Tan, research manager at investment house Vickers Ballas Research.
Tan Geok Hock, a Schroder Research analyst, said: "If you're doing cars already, motorcycles and vans are not a quantum leap. They're just a natural progression."
Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, key proponent of the vehicle projects, will launch the 110 cc motorcycle at a plant in Gurun, in his northern home state of Kedah.
Like other Malaysian-made vehicles, foreign partnerships are the key, analysts said.
The motorcycle's manufacturer, Motosikal dan Enjin Nasional Sdn Bhd (Modenas), is a 600 million ringgit ($240 million) joint venture between two Malaysian and two Japanese partners.

Malaysian automotive group Diversified Resources Bhd has a 55 percent stake, the federal government's investment agency Khazanah Nasional 15 percent, Kawasaki Heavy Industries Ltd 19 percent, and Nissho-Iwai Corp 11 percent.

Modenas officials said they expect the motorcycle to be priced under 4,000 ringgit ($1,600) with first-year production of 100,000 units. Analysts are expecting brisk sales due to its competitive pricing.

"If they price it below 4,000 ringgit, I think it will do well," said an auto analyst at stockbrokers WI Carr (Malaysia), who declined to be named. He said similar imported motorcycles are priced from 4,100 to 4,500 ringgit.
Modenas' main shareholder, Diversified Resources or DRB, is experienced at vehicle production and marketing.
DRB, owned by Malaysian Yahaya Ahmad, controls the country's first national car maker, Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton), through heavy industrial group Hicom Holdings Bhd.

Cars made by Proton dominate the local vehicle market, accounting for about 53 percent of sales in the first half of 1996. Proton makes the cars with help from its Japanese partner, Mitsubishi Motors Corp.
Proton and French company Automobiles Citroen, also jointly produce the smaller Proton Tiara car.

Malaysia's second national car company, Perusahaan Otomobil Kedua Sdn Bhd (Perodua), has Japanese partners in Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd and Mitsui & Co Ltd. Perodua makes a sub-compact car and a national van.
Last month, three Malaysian companies, including Berjaya Group Bhd, joined Korea's Hyundai Motor Co Ltd and France's Renault SA to build a heavy-duty van and a light truck.
DRB, Hicom and Japan's Isuzu Motors Ltd are also planning to build trucks and buses locally.
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-201 4813)
($1 = 2.50 ringgit)
